title: Saving Our Planet
paragraphs: Climate change is one of the biggest challenges of our time. Temperatures are rising, glaciers are melting, and extreme weather events are becoming more frequent. Scientists agree that human activity — especially the burning of fossil fuels — is the main cause.

Kazakhstan is particularly affected by environmental change. The Aral Sea, once the fourth largest lake in the world, has almost completely dried up due to irrigation projects in the twentieth century. This is considered one of the greatest environmental disasters in history.

But there is hope. Renewable energy sources — solar, wind, and hydroelectric power — are being developed around the world. In Kazakhstan, the government has committed to producing 15% of its electricity from renewable sources by 2030.

Many young people are taking action. At WKU, students have formed an Eco Club. They organise tree-planting events, recycling campaigns, and awareness programmes. 'Every action counts,' says the club president, Zhibek Akhmetova.

Individual changes matter too. Plastic bags are being replaced by reusable ones. Public transport is being expanded in major cities. Many products are now made from recycled materials. Each small step adds up.

The environment is not just a science issue — it is an economic and social issue. If we don't act now, the costs in the future will be enormous. As Zhibek says: 'We don't inherit the Earth from our ancestors — we borrow it from our children.'

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Did you know that plastic is produced in huge quantities every year, and most of it is never recycled?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I know — it's terrifying. What can we do as students?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Small things make a difference. Carry a reusable bottle. Use public transport. Sort your rubbish.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Our Eco Club is organising a clean-up day next Saturday. Will you come?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Of course! The river near campus is being polluted — we need to act.
